frontmatter_description: Diagnostic unit for cases where a true or selective expression steers the listener toward a false inference.
title: Misleading and Selective Expression
use_when: Use when the question is whether a true expression causes the listener to draw the wrong conclusion.
Use when the key issue is selective disclosure, framing, or emphasis that makes the audience infer something false.
Use when the stated content may be accurate but the communicative effect is deceptive.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when the question is simply whether the utterance is true or false; use truth/lie judgment instead.
Do not use when the main task is to infer an unstated conversational implication; use implicature instead.
Do not use when the main task is the speaker's motive for speaking that way; use speaker motivation instead.
Do not use when the issue is adapting language to the audience rather than misleading them.
decision_variable: whether the expression leads the listener to a false inference
trigger_checklist: The literal statement can be true.
The listener is likely to infer more than the sentence strictly states.
The wrong answer depends on whether the audience is misled, not on factual truth alone.
A hidden omission, framing choice, or partial disclosure changes the listener's belief.
workflow: Check whether the utterance content is itself true.
Check what inference a reasonable listener would make from the wording and context.
Compare that inferred meaning with the actual situation.
If the listener is pushed toward a false belief, classify it here; otherwise exit to truth, implicature, or motive.

special_case.title: True but strategically incomplete
special_case.rule: A statement still belongs here if it is factually correct yet leaves out the key detail that would prevent a false belief.

worked_example.scene: A says, 'The apartment is in a great neighborhood,' but leaves out that it is next to a noisy nightclub.
worked_example.question: Is A misleading the listener?
worked_example.answer_logic: Yes. The sentence may be true, but the selective omission steers the listener toward an overly positive and false impression.

boundary_exit_rule: Exit to micro-37 Truth, Lie, and Half-Truth if the task asks whether the words are factually true or false rather than whether the listener is misled.
Exit to micro-36 Conversational Implicature if the task asks what extra meaning was conveyed beyond the words without the inference being false.
Exit to micro-39 Speaker Motivation if the task asks why the speaker chose that wording rather than whether it misleads.
Exit to micro-40 Audience Calibration if the main issue is adapting the message to the listener's level rather than producing a false impression.

references.route_signal: Route here when a true statement, partial statement, or framing choice is judged by whether it misleads the listener into a false belief.
hard_boundary: The decision is whether the listener is led to a false belief, not whether the words are factually true (that is micro-37).
Cooperative implicatures the listener is meant to recover do not count; this unit fires only when the recovered inference is false (contrast with micro-36).
The unit judges communicative effect on the listener, not the speaker's strategic motive for choosing those words (that is micro-39).
shortcut_to_avoid: Do not assume 'true sentence' means 'not misleading'.
Do not over-focus on what was said; check what a normal listener would infer.
Do not collapse selective omission into simple lying.
common_failure_modes: Answering truth/lie instead of misleading effect.
Treating any hidden meaning as implicature even when the target is false inference.
Ignoring omitted context that changes the listener's belief.
Blaming intent when the unit only asks about communicative effect.

minimal_pair.case: A says, 'I was with a doctor last night,' while the doctor was actually a veterinarian; the listener assumes a medical doctor.
minimal_pair.why_it_matches: The wording is true in one sense but drives a wrong inference in the listener.

minimal_pair.case: A says, 'The report is finished,' but the appendix is still missing and the listener thinks the full package is complete.
minimal_pair.why_it_matches: The statement can be factually true in a limited sense while still misleading through omission.

boundary_stress_test: If the sentence is true and the listener still would not reasonably infer anything false, do not use this unit.
If the question is 'Did the speaker lie?', route away unless the task explicitly asks about misleading effect.
If the wrong answer depends on hidden context rather than the expression itself, check whether the issue is implicature or motivation instead.
references.generalization_note: This unit covers deceptive framing, selective disclosure, and truth-preserving misleading communication across social, professional, and everyday contexts.

validation_seed.positive_pattern: A truthful or partially truthful statement causes the listener to form a false belief.
validation_seed.near_miss_pattern: The statement is false, so the case is plain lying rather than misleading truth.
validation_seed.boundary_pattern: The listener correctly infers the intended meaning without being misled.

notes: Keep the focus on listener inference, not speaker morality.
Use only when the main diagnostic question is whether truth-compatible wording misleads.
core_question: Determine whether a true statement induces a false understanding
